static_traits.name: Courtney
static_traits.social_status: Has a few friends to talk to, but has not yet discussed the fear with them; the rest not disclosed
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar fear before; has not yet received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, fairly cooperative; able to describe trigger situations and bodily reactions; says trying to comfort self with logic and safety measures but with limited effect; neutral attitude; speech rate not mentioned

basic_info.main_problem: My fear of falling and dying while rock climbing markedly affects my ability to enjoy climbing. The fear began after a close friend had a climbing accident a few months ago and has kept worsening; strong fear and anxiety appear whenever thinking of or planning to climb, making it hard to take part in the activity.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize the fear of falling and dying is stopping me from enjoying beloved climbing, so I hope to work through this problem in counseling and enjoy climbing again.
growth_experiences: A few months ago, a close friend had a climbing accident. This incident made me strongly worry about climbing safety, and stress levels rose markedly. Since then, strong fear and anxiety appear whenever seeing a rock face, recalling the accident, or planning to climb; it has become gradually hard to enjoy and take part in climbing.

core_beliefs: Rock climbing is highly dangerous; I will very likely slip, fall, and die
Even with safety measures, serious accidents cannot truly be avoided

special_situations.event: Gazing at the rock wall before climbing or being in a climbing setting
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I start climbing, I will very likely slip, fall, and suffer serious injury or even death
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Tries to focus on safety measures and rationalize risks, postpones or avoids climbing
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time something will very likely go wrong; I will fall and die

special_situations.event: When planning a rock-climbing activity (checking routes, inviting companions, preparing equipment)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I go climbing, the worst case will surely happen in the future
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Canceling or weakening plans, constantly rehearsing dangerous scenarios in the mind as self-'reminders' to avoid them
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how I prepare, a terrible accident will happen in the end

special_situations.event: Recalling a friend's rock-climbing accident months ago
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If they had an accident, I am also very likely to suffer similar serious consequences
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Using the friend's accident as evidence to reinforce my judgment of the risk, reducing exposure to climbing-related information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: She had an accident; sooner or later the same thing will happen to me

special_situations.event: Thinks about safety measures but emotions remain high
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I feel intense fear, it means the danger is indeed great
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Doubles the use of rationality and safety checklists to suppress emotional reactions
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am so scared; it must be because it really is dangerous

core_conflict.wish: Longing to freely enjoy beloved rock climbing on the premise of ensuring safety, and to be accepted by peers rather than seen as weak
core_conflict.fear: Fear of encountering uncontrollable danger and getting hurt or dying while pursuing climbing; also fear of being judged after exposing vulnerability, seen as weak by friends
defense_goal: Lowering danger and anxiety by avoiding climbing or postponing plans
Appearing strong and not revealing fear to avoid being seen as weak
Weakening emotions by emphasizing safety details through intellectualization

object_relations.self_representation: A rock climber who needs to hide vulnerability, worried about being seen as weak
object_relations.object_representation: Friends may judge or look down on my vulnerability

object_relations.self_representation: An individual vulnerable to harm in dangerous situations
object_relations.object_representation: The climbing environment / rock face as an uncontrollable, deadly dangerous object

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether they are willing to share their fears and vulnerability with friends
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If I voice my fear, friends will think me weak and look down on me (transference: projecting inner self-judgment onto others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Respond briefly in a calm, restrained tone, displacing the topic to neutral content, avoiding emotional vocabulary and detail exposure.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about climbing risks or recalling the friend's accident, as anxiety rises
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing only more facts and rules can keep control and safety (transference: projecting insecurity onto the environment and countering it with rationality and rules)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Uses expert-style, data-based language to list safety checklists and probabilities, tone restrained, avoiding the level of feelings, focusing on 'facts' and 'steps'.

manifestations: The friend's climbing accident triggered strong worries about falling and dying
Worst-case fantasies about death every time climbing is planned or thought of
outcomes: Avoiding or being unable to take part in climbing
Decreased enjoyment of life; other activities also become tense

manifestations: Unwilling to share the fear with friends for fear of seeming weak
Keeps silent on important issues and reduces help-seeking
outcomes: The support system has difficulty functioning

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Worrying about 'looking weak', overly concerned with others' evaluations, unwilling to speak
Overly cautious when sharing emotions and seeking support

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves.
manifestations: Withdrawing the urge to seek support from friends, not expressing fear outward
Channeling energy into self-repression and inner digestion rather than outside help

positive_force: Loves rock climbing, with sustained motivation
Having some friend resources to talk to (though not yet utilized)
Willing to seek help and enter counseling, showing motivation to change
Can try using rationality and safety measures to manage fear
Hopeful about the treatment plan, willing to record triggers and bodily reactions
negative_force: Marked catastrophizing and predicting-the-future cognitive patterns
Overgeneralization from the friend's accident reinforces the sense of danger
Avoidant behavior reduces opportunities for corrective experiences
Unwillingness to expose vulnerability limits access to social support
Anxiety generalizing to other activities, lowering enjoyment of life

target_behavior.behavior: Intense fear of and avoidance of climbing (with anxiety, physiological arousal)
antecedent: Gazing at the rock wall or being in a climbing scene
Plans a rock climbing activity (checks routes, prepares gear)
Recalling a friend's rock climbing accident
target_behavior.core_reason: Catastrophizing about falling and death and 'predicting the future' cognitions formed after the friend's climbing accident; emotional reasoning maintains and worsens the fear
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential danger and intense anxiety, maintaining subjective safety and control
target_behavior.consequence: Unable to take part in and enjoy climbing, decreased enjoyment of life; tension and excessive rumination generalizing to other activities, affecting daily life
